- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% to prevent overreaction.
- If model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d window (first 5–7 days), apply a +1.5 to +3.0% upward bias to capture initial momentum.
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0) and price is trending up, model often lags — add 1–3 days of delayed upward adjustment in forecast.
- If model forecast mean is consistently below true outcome mean over 30d, apply a +2% to +5% global upward shift to correct for systematic underestimation.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in recent 5 days), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±1–2% deviation in short-term (1–3 day) predictions to reflect uncertainty.
